Add Zplot Density Lines

Source: R/zplot-api.R
lines.zplot_brma.Rd

Adds model-implied density lines to an existing zplot.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'zplot_brma'
lines(
  x,
  plot_type = "base",
  probs = c(0.025, 0.975),
  max_samples = if (inherits(x, "brma.mv")) 1000 else 10000,
  plot_ci = TRUE,
  extrapolate = FALSE,
  from = -6,
  to = 6,
  by = 0.05,
  length.out = NULL,
  col = "black",
  as_data = FALSE,
  integration_control = x[["zplot"]][["data"]][["integration_control"]],
  parallel = FALSE,
  cores = min(4, RoBMA.get_option("max_cores")),
  ...
)

Arguments

x

a zplot_brma object.

plot_type

graphics system: "base" or "ggplot". Defaults to "base".

probs

quantiles for credible intervals. Defaults to c(.025, .975). The bands are pointwise Harrell-Davis quantiles of the posterior density draws (see Details).

max_samples

maximum posterior samples for density. Defaults to 1000 for brma.mv models and 10000 for other models. Use Inf to use all posterior samples. This plotting budget does not change the EDR and missing-study summaries stored by as_zplot().

plot_ci

whether to show credible interval bands. Defaults to TRUE.

extrapolate

whether to remove bias adjustments. Defaults to FALSE.

from, to

z-value range for density. Defaults to -6 and 6.

by

step size for density points. Defaults to 0.05.

length.out

number of density points (alternative to by).

col

line color. Defaults to "black".

as_data

whether to return data instead of plotting. Defaults to FALSE.

integration_control

numerical integration settings created by set_selection_likelihood_control(). Defaults to the settings stored by as_zplot(); an explicit value overrides them for these lines. Legacy objects without stored settings require an explicit control, or recreation with as_zplot(), when their selected density needs integration.

parallel

whether to distribute multivariate selection-model density calculations across local workers. Defaults to FALSE. Only posterior draws are divided; the full publication event and integration settings are retained. Scalar models, Gaussian-reference-only curves, and EDR summaries remain serial.

cores

number of local workers when parallel = TRUE. Defaults to the smaller of 4 and RoBMA.get_option("max_cores"). One core or fewer posterior draws than workers uses serial computation. Parallel workers require matching installed package/native builds and share the configured selection-cache budget. Worker count is reported when parallel work starts.

...

additional graphical parameters.

Value

NULL invisibly for base graphics, ggplot2 layers for ggplot, or a data frame with columns x, y, y_lCI, y_uCI if as_data = TRUE.

Details

The density uses the conditioning_depth stored by as_zplot(). Recreate the zplot object to change the predictive target.

The line is the posterior mean of the density at each z value, and its credible band (plot_ci = TRUE, or y_lCI and y_uCI of the returned data) is formed by pointwise Harrell-Davis quantiles of the posterior density draws at the probabilities probs, computed by BayesTools::harrell_davis_quantile(). They estimate the same quantiles as the empirical quantiles of the draws but smooth the kinks that the empirical quantiles show along z. The bands remain pointwise, and, because every draw contributes, they can differ visibly from the empirical quantiles when few draws are used (max_samples below a few hundred). Near the edge of a point mass in the draws (e.g., draws of models that fix the plotted quantity in a model-averaged posterior) the band blends the point mass and the remaining draws, and extreme probabilities (e.g., probs = c(.0005, .9995)) are not estimated more accurately than by the empirical quantiles; see BayesTools::harrell_davis_quantile() for these caveats.

When extrapolate = FALSE, the density includes all bias adjustments (PET/PEESE regression, selection weights) representing the fitted model. When extrapolate = TRUE, bias adjustments are removed to show the hypothetical distribution without publication bias. Multivariate models, retained estimate-level or sampling-error sources, applicable integrated contexts, and best-rule selection models use a normalized pre-selection Gaussian reference. Released univariate product targets retain inverse-weight scaling and their extrapolated curve need not integrate to one.

See also

plot.zplot_brma(), hist.zplot_brma()
